references.text: The Lord stood at the top of the ladder and spoke to Jacob, giving him promises about the land, descendants, and blessing – the immediate continuation of the dream.
Jacob wakes up and calls the place 'the house of God' and 'the gate of heaven,' as a direct response to the dream of the ladder between heaven and earth.
God appears again to Jacob at Bethel, where Jacob originally had the dream, and confirms the promises given to him.
God's angels are commanded to protect believers, which recalls the angels who go up and down on the ladder in Jacob's dream.

Jesus refers directly to Jacob's dream when he tells Nathanael that he will see heaven opened and God's angels ascending and descending above the Son of Man, pointing to Christ as the connection between heaven and earth.
The angels are described as ministering spirits sent to serve those who will inherit salvation, relevant to the angels going up and down on the ladder.
